content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xml catalogs within Advanced XML Specifications and Technologies. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XML Catalogs matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about purpose of catalogs, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: These related specifications extend how XML documents refer to external resources, address fragments, represent links, or define a logical information model. They are optional specialist tools rather than requirements for every XML application.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Purpose of catalogs; Mapping public and system identifiers; Resolving external resources locally; Reproducible processing environments. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.
